question.problem:
Given that the function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}x+\sqrt{x}, & 0\le x<4 \\ x+c, & x\ge 4\end{aligned}
$$

is continuous at $x=4,$ find the value of the constant $c.$
question.worked_solution:
At $x=4,$ the left-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}(x+\sqrt{x}) \\  & =4+\sqrt{4} \\  & =6,\end{aligned}
$$

and the right-sided limit is

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}f(x) & =f(4) \\  & =4+c.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x=4,$ we require that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {4}^{-}}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to {4}^{+}}f(x) \\ 6 & =4+c \\ c & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
